reuse.why: The link guards are factored into link.ts and called from every provider, and findOrCreateBank is reused, but the Fintegra link and download functions are new copies of the Akahu ones, and the takeover clears fields itself instead of reusing unlinkAccount's local part.

duplication.why: linkFintegraAccount repeats linkAkahuAccount's whole upgrade/insert/payee/sync/notify flow, downloadFintegraTransactions repeats the Akahu/Pluggy download, and the eight-field reset in assertAccountNotLinked copies unlinkAccount's update.

placement.why: The link rules sit well in accounts/link.ts and the provider wiring follows existing files, but a function named assertAccountNotLinked now unlinks other accounts, mixing a guard with a mutation.

scope.why: Edits serve the four steps; widening DbAccount.account_sync_source to all providers is a small side cleanup.

maintainability.why: One definition each for the closed-account and already-linked rules helps, but a sixth copy of the provider link flow, another copy of the download function and an assert with side effects will drift.

bypasses_abstraction.where: assertAccountNotLinked in accounts/link.ts clears the old account with db.updateAccount instead of going through (a local part of) unlinkAccount in accounts/app.ts

disguised_duplication.where: downloadFintegraTransactions is the Akahu download compacted into fewer lines and with its error branch dropped; linkFintegraAccount is linkAkahuAccount with an inlined institution: reshaped copies rather than shared code

abstraction_drift.where: link.assertAccountNotLinked gained the replaceExistingLink parameter and a branch that turns the guard into an unlink; all six link functions call both guards
